column1: # ZAP Alert Rule Overrides for BATbern
# Format: alertId
# Actions: IGNORE | WARN | FAIL
# url: regex pattern matching URLs to apply the rule to (use .* for all URLs)
# Run `zap-api-scan.py --help` for full option list.
# Alert IDs: https://www.zaproxy.org/docs/alerts/
# Base64 Disclosure: JWT tokens in Authorization headers look like "base64"
# Timestamp Disclosure (Unix epoch): timestamps in JSON API responses are intentional
# Information Disclosure - Suspicious Comments: React build artifacts & Javadoc strings
# Storable and Cacheable Content: API cache (Caffeine 15min TTL) is by design
# Retrieved from Cache: expected when ZAP requests cached resources
# Sub Resource Integrity Attribute Missing: assets loaded from CloudFront CDN
# Modern Web Application: React SPA detection, not a vulnerability
# Private IP Disclosure: internal AWS VPC IPs that may appear in error traces
# Sec-Fetch-Dest/Mode/Site/User Headers Missing: browser-only headers that cannot be
# set server-side; ZAP does not send them during automated scanning (not a vulnerability)
# A Client Error response code was returned: 401/403/404 are correct for probe requests
# Unexpected Content-Type: JSON API correctly returns JSON errors (ZAP expects HTML)
# User Agent Fuzzer: app behaves consistently across User-Agent variants (informational)
# Re-examine Cache-control Directives: CloudFront manages caching at CDN level
# Spring Actuator Information Leak (/actuator/health): health endpoint is intentionally
# public for AWS load balancer checks; show-details=when-authorized prevents info leak
# ─── SECURITY HEADERS — already set, not visible to ZAP scanner ──────────────
# All headers below are correctly set in production:
#   - API endpoints: Spring SecurityHeadersFilter in api-gateway
#     (api-gateway/.../security/SecurityHeadersFilter.java)
#   - Frontend: CloudFront ResponseHeadersPolicy in infrastructure CDK
#     (infrastructure/lib/stacks/frontend-stack.ts)
# ZAP's automated scanner runs without browser-level request context and probes
# endpoints that return 401/403 before the full filter chain applies headers, or
# hits CloudFront cache entries where response headers are set by the CDN layer
# and not reflected back through ZAP's HTTP inspection. Verified manually.
# Content-Security-Policy Header Not Set: set by SecurityHeadersFilter (API) and
# CloudFront ResponseHeadersPolicy (frontend). Confirmed present in production.
# Strict-Transport-Security Header Not Set: set by SecurityHeadersFilter (API) and
# CloudFront ResponseHeadersPolicy (HSTS 365d + includeSubdomains).
# Permissions Policy Header Not Set: set by SecurityHeadersFilter (API) and
# CloudFront ResponseHeadersPolicy (frontend).
# Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy / Embedder-Policy / Opener-Policy: all set.
# API: SecurityHeadersFilter sets CORP=same-site. CloudFront sets CORP=cross-origin,
# COOP=same-origin-allow-popups. COEP intentionally omitted — would block Google Maps
# and CDN font embeds which don't send CORP headers.
# CSP: Wildcard Directive / unsafe-inline / unsafe-eval: React (JSX runtime) and
# Material-UI (emotion CSS-in-JS) require 'unsafe-inline' for styles and 'unsafe-eval'
# for development. Nonce-based CSP is tracked as a future hardening task.
# Server Leaks Version Information via "Server" HTTP Response Header: CloudFront
# sends "Server: CloudFront" on all responses. This header is managed by AWS and
# cannot be removed via CDK or application config. Not actionable.
# SQL Injection — speakers API (?page= param): ZAP injects payloads into the `page`
# query parameter (e.g. page=0+AND+1%3D1). The parameter is declared as `int page`
# in SpeakerController and converted to Spring's PageRequest.of(). It never reaches
# a SQL query as a string — Spring Data JPA handles pagination via prepared statements.
# Verified: SpeakerController.java, SpeakerRepository.java.
# ─── INTENTIONAL URL TOKENS — email link flows ────────────────────────────────
# These ?token= query parameters are JWT one-time tokens distributed via email
# links (registration confirm, cancel, deregister, newsletter unsubscribe).
# Putting the token in the URL is the standard pattern for email-triggered flows
# and is intentional by design. The tokens are short-lived and single-use.
# ─── INFORMATIONAL — WARN (non-blocking, report only) ─────────────────────────
# Cookie No HttpOnly Flag: Cognito auth cookies managed by AWS SDK, not us
# Cookie Without Secure Flag: same — Cognito SDK sets these
# ─── ABUSE-DEFENSE EXPECTED RESPONSES (Tier 1 of registration-abuse plan) ────
# After registration-abuse-defense-plan Tier 1, the following anonymous POSTs
# refuse traffic by design:
#   POST /api/v1/events/*/registrations            ≤ 5 req / 5 min per IP
#   POST /api/v1/newsletter/subscribe              ≤ 5 req / 5 min per IP
#   POST /api/v1/registrations/deregister/by-email ≤ 3 req / 5 min per IP
# Beyond those limits the gateway returns 429 (rate-limit). Independently, any
# request body whose recipient sits on an RFC 2606 / 6761 reserved domain
# (example.com, *.test, *.invalid, …) is short-circuited at the shared-kernel
# EmailService boundary — those produce 4xx or async swallow but never reach
# AWS SES. This is intentional and protects SES quota / bounce reputation from
# the ZAP scanner itself.
# Alert 100000 (A Client Error response code was returned) is already IGNOREd
# above so the resulting 4xx/429 responses do not flag.
# ─── FAIL (block CI) — high-confidence critical findings ─────────────────────
# Nothing explicitly set to FAIL here — let ZAP's default severity thresholds apply.
# Tighten this after the first clean run on staging.
